title: Theseus — Echoes in later ages
summary: Theseus slew the Minotaur in the Labyrinth of Crete with Ariadne's thread. This study traces the myth's afterlife.
body:
Theseus slew the Minotaur in the Labyrinth of Crete with Ariadne's thread. He became the legendary king and unifier of Athens.

Long after its gods lost worshippers, Theseus kept working — in Renaissance painting, in Romantic poetry, in modern film. Each age found its own anxieties reflected in the old story. Viewed through a narrative lens, Theseus is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

Myths survive by being reusable. Theseus proved endlessly reusable. A fifth sub-question considers how children first meet Theseus, and what the simplified versions leave out. Related entries in this archive: Maat and Horus.
key_points: Afterlife of Theseus through the centuries.
